agentCan: Implement the authorization code flow, JWKS validation of the large JWT access tokens, and rotating-refresh persistence
Register redirect URIs and generate the client secret flow in the portal steps

approval.cost: No fee is stated anywhere in the docs read
approval.trigger: 'Applications you create are initially limited to private access only. You can only grant access to new applications using the Constant Contact user that created the application. In order to allow all Constant Contact users to grant access to your application, contact support by calling 866-289-2101 to begin the approval process.' The documented process is that phone call; the docs publish no criteria, no checklist, no submission portal, and no timeline for the approval. Pre-approval cap: effectively one user (the application's creator), which is your entire test population until approval. No self-serve marketplace listing process is described in the developer documentation read.
approval.wait: Not stated (the process starts with a support call; no duration given)

blockers.detail: Everything works in testing with your own user, which makes it easy to build the whole integration before discovering that no customer can authorize it until the support-driven approval completes, on an unpublished timeline with unpublished criteria.
blockers.howToClear: Call support (866-289-2101) at the START of the project, not the end, and build against your creator user while approval proceeds.
blockers.title: The private-access gate is the launch blocker

blockers.detail: You pick the OAuth2 setting (Authorization Code/Implicit, PKCE, or Device) and the refresh-token method (Rotating, recommended 'for use with most applications because they are most secure', or Long Lived) in the New Application dialog. With rotating tokens, each refresh returns a new refresh token, so you must persist the replacement every time or strand the connection. Whether these settings can be changed on an existing application or require a new one is not stated in the pages read.
blockers.howToClear: Choose for your client type at creation (Authorization Code + Rotating for a server web app) and treat the choice as permanent.
blockers.title: Flow and refresh-method choices are creation-time settings

blockers.detail: offline_access is a scope like any other and easy to omit; without it there is no refresh token and users must re-authenticate and reauthorize when the 24-hour access token expires. Consent is all-or-nothing: 'The account owner or authorized user must either grant access to all of your scopes or decline access to your application', so requesting fewer scopes is the only adoption lever.
blockers.howToClear: Always include offline_access and request only the scopes you need.
blockers.title: No offline_access scope, no refresh token

alternatives: PKCE Flow (public clients: native/single-page apps that cannot safely store a secret; refresh tokens supported)
Device Authorization Flow (input-constrained/browserless apps; refresh tokens supported)
Implicit Flow (legacy only: 'Use only if your application already uses the Implicit flow or does not support Web Crypto'; refresh tokens NOT supported)
flavor.recommended: Authorization Code Flow with Rotating Refresh Tokens and the offline_access scope
flavor.why: The object is an application registered in the V3 API Developer Portal under My Applications. Registering yields an API Key (this is the client_id) and, on demand, a client secret. The docs position the Authorization Code Flow for 'traditional web applications (your application runs on a web server) and is able to safely store the client secret' and call it 'the most secure OAuth2 flow' because the access token passes directly to your server, never the browser. Rotating Refresh Tokens are 'recommended for use with most applications because they are most secure'. Scopes (V3): account_read, account_update, contact_data, campaign_data, plus offline_access (required to receive a refresh token).

humanMust: Sign up for a V3 developer account in the Developer Portal (a trial Constant Contact account is created for development/testing)
Register the application and make the creation-time flow and refresh-method choices
Generate the client secret and copy it immediately ('The secret only appears once, when you first request to generate it')
Phone Constant Contact support (866-289-2101) to begin the approval process before onboarding real users
name: Constant Contact
nuances: Token lifetimes: access tokens 'expire after 1440 minutes (86,400 seconds). They have a maximum life of 24 hours' (Implicit: 480 minutes / 8 hours). Refresh tokens 'are 42 characters long and expire after 180 days, if never used'. Authorization codes 'expire after 5 minutes (300 seconds)' and can be used once. Doc inconsistency: the Authorization Code Flow page's example token response shows expires_in: 28800 (8 hours) while its own text and the OAuth2 Overview state 86,400 seconds / 24 hours; code defensively to the expires_in you actually receive.

'Constant Contact rate limits the Token endpoint. A 429 response will likely be returned if you attempt to refresh an access token before every V3 API request.' Refresh only when the existing token is expired or about to expire (docs suggest treating a token as expired when its expiry is within 5 minutes).

Access tokens are large JWTs (1,000-1,200 characters) with mandatory validation work: validate signature and claims against Constant Contact's JWKS for every new access token (expected issuer and audience documented; cid must equal your API key; platform_user_id uniquely identifies the user).

Redirect URI rules: 'Wildcards are not supported except at the domain root level.' Registration does not validate the URI; a mismatch between the authorization request and the registered URIs returns a 400 at authorization time instead, so misconfigurations surface late, with real users.
Legacy V2 is a different world: different keys and flows, no scope parameter. The current program is V3-only (V3 keys required); don't mix V2 documentation into a V3 build.
prerequisites: A V3 developer account in the Developer Portal (signup creates a trial Constant Contact account for development/testing)
Redirect URI(s) to register on the application (multiple are supported)
The flow and refresh-method decisions made before clicking Create

steps.detail: My Applications > Sign up (email, password, name, organization, phone). A trial Constant Contact account is created for development/testing.
steps.title: Sign up for a V3 developer account

steps.detail: My Applications > New Application: enter the app name (shown to users on the grant-access prompt), choose the OAuth2 setting (Authorization Code/Implicit, PKCE, or Device) and the refresh-token method (Rotating recommended, or Long Lived), then Create. Both choices are made at creation.
steps.title: Register the application (choose flow + refresh method)

steps.detail: Click edit on the app: the API Key (client_id) shows in the Details view. If your flow needs a secret, click Generate Client Secret and copy it immediately ('The secret only appears once'). Register your redirect URI(s). Click Save.
steps.title: Get credentials; register redirect URIs

steps.detail: GET authz.constantcontact.com/oauth2/default/v1/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state (required), and optional scope (space-delimited, include offline_access), nonce, prompt=login. The user sees the Permission Request screen listing your scopes and grants or declines (all-or-nothing).
steps.title: Build the authorization request

steps.detail: POST authz.constantcontact.com/oauth2/default/v1/token with code, redirect_uri, grant_type=authorization_code, Basic auth base64(client_id:client_secret), form-encoded. Response: access_token (JWT), refresh_token (only if offline_access was granted), id_token, scope, expires_in. Validate each new access token's signature and claims against the JWKS, then call the V3 API with Authorization: Bearer.
steps.title: Exchange the code; validate tokens; call the API

steps.detail: POST the token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token and Basic auth. With rotating tokens, persist the new refresh token every time. Refresh only when the token is expired or near expiry: the token endpoint is rate-limited and 429s aggressive refreshers.
steps.title: Refresh (sparingly)

steps.detail: 'In order to allow all Constant Contact users to grant access to your application, contact support by calling 866-289-2101 to begin the approval process.' Until approval completes, only the user who created the application can grant it access.
steps.title: Start the approval process (phone support) before onboarding users

tagline: Standard, well-documented OAuth 2.0, except every new application starts private to its creator alone: real customers cannot connect until you phone Constant Contact support and complete an approval process whose criteria and timeline the docs never publish.

time.active: ~15 min of portal setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow and token-validation code
time.total: Unknown: approval duration is not stated
